habitat: Mostly well-developed riverine forest and large-tree woodland fringing lakes, also mixed bushveld. It roosts by day in dense thickets and is less often seen by day than Pearl-spotted Owlet.
summary: A common resident. Slightly larger and more dumpy than Pearl-spotted Owlet. The upperparts are finely barred, the wings have a row of bold white spots, and the underparts are white with brown spots in rows. The call is an urgent repeated kerrooo. The Kemp name Barred Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Pearl-spotted Owlet is smaller, with white spots rather than fine barring above, and two black marks on the nape.

head.pattern: Head included in the dark brown-grey upperparts, with fine white barring.

upperparts.pattern: Dark brown-grey above, finely barred, with a band of large white wing spots.

underparts.pattern: White below with grey-brown bars and spots. The description says brown spots arranged in rows.

wings.pattern: A row of bold white spots reaches the shoulder.

viewNotes.note: White underparts with brown spots arranged in rows.
Dumpy, with fine barring above and a row of bold white wing spots.
Flight plumage is not described apart from the white wing spots.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: An urgent 'kerrooo-kerrooo-krrooo…', or 'krrooo-trrooo' repeated many times. The grade A call is from Hoedspruit. The filename is XC358211-Barred Owlet ZOOM0013.MP3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Dark brown-grey and grey-brown are not stored as single colours. The grade A call is from Hoedspruit. The Kemp name Barred Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.
